summary: CLI writes resolved absolute flumeDir/configDir back into process.env.FLUME_DIR/FLUME_CONFIG_DIR so the chain + spawned children read one canonical state root

edit.description: After resolving flumeDir/configDir, assign the absolute resolved paths back to process.env per §12 (build lane); extract the resolver if needed for testability (§14).
Sessions-track-flumeDir closure under `### Fixed`, citing 0.3.0 per §6.

tests.asserts: At the resolution seam, process.env.FLUME_DIR/FLUME_CONFIG_DIR hold the absolute resolved root for both env-unset (default) and env-set-relative cases per §14.

acceptance: process.env.FLUME_DIR/FLUME_CONFIG_DIR are absolute-canonical after resolution; the dogfood chain's `?? CHAIN_DIR` fallback is never hit in normal operation; pnpm test green.
notes: Linchpin: chore 20940b8 already points sessions at process.env.FLUME_DIR and explicitly relies on this build-lane canonicalization. Until it lands the one-rm teardown promise leaks when FLUME_DIR is unset or relative.

summary: loadChainModule drops a chain-exported forkResolver; extract it like `agent` so the stock-CLI governor adoption path documented in §3 actually works

edit.description: loadChainModule (currently extracts only chain+agent, src/Dispatcher.ts:182,191) must also surface ns.forkResolver / interop d.forkResolver into the returned ChainModule per §3.

tests.asserts: A chain.ts exporting forkResolver has it picked up per tick and govern selection (overrides DispatcherOptions.forkResolver), exactly as `agent` does.

acceptance: A chain module exporting forkResolver governs fork pickability; ChainModule.forkResolver is no longer always undefined at runtime; test green.
notes: Confirmed bug, not just untested: type+doc (Dispatcher.ts:121-132) promise the export; impl (line 191) returns without it, so tick()'s `chainModule.forkResolver ?? opts.forkResolver` can never see a chain export. Breaks §3's stock-CLI bridge.

summary: Add §7's three uncovered governor tests: predicate-flip makes a fork-blocked entry pickable, no-resolver selection ≡ v0.2, forkResolver invoked once per tick with repoRoot

edit.description: Add the three §7 cases the governor commit left uncovered (predicate-flip, no-resolver≡v0.2, once-per-tick-with-repoRoot).

tests.asserts: Fork-blocked entry becomes pickable next tick when the predicate flips to resolved; with no forkResolver selection is byte-identical to v0.2; forkResolver is called once per tick with the repo root.

acceptance: All three §7 cases present and green; no behavior change to src/.
notes: Schema/seam/skip tests already exist (tests/PendingSchema.test.ts, tests/Dispatcher.test.ts:780-902). Only these three §7 bullets are missing.

summary: Assert a child `flume tick` spawned by the supervisor observes the supervisor's FLUME_DIR/FLUME_CONFIG_DIR end-to-end (the §11 env-inheritance claim)

edit.description: Add a case: a child tick inherits the supervisor's canonical FLUME_DIR/FLUME_CONFIG_DIR via env (defaultTickRunner spawns with no env override) per §14.

tests.asserts: A spawned `flume tick` sees the supervisor's FLUME_DIR/FLUME_CONFIG_DIR values, confirming loop→tick inheritance end-to-end.

acceptance: Subprocess test proves env inheritance of the canonical roots across the loop→tick boundary; green.
notes: Existing file tests chain reload only, not env inheritance. Blocked on canonicalization so the inherited value under test is the absolute resolved root, not a raw/unset var.

summary: Document FLUME_DIR/FLUME_CONFIG_DIR + attach-work-detach + one-`rm` teardown (README) and the chain-author session-placement requirement, dogfood chain as worked example (CHAIN-AUTHORING)

Document the chain-author requirement: per-run artifacts (sessions, etc.) must live under process.env.FLUME_DIR; cite the dogfood chain (§12) as the worked example (§13).

acceptance: README + CHAIN-AUTHORING describe the relocation surface, the outside-the-repo dock posture, and the chain-author requirement, matching shipped behavior.
